title: Add jurisdictional-access-evaluator to installer: RBAC v2 constraint language, KMS scope gates, and audit redactor
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: Adds installer-level jurisdictional policy evaluation and KMS scoping; enforces RBAC v2 constraints on operator credentials; audit redaction for PII during onboarding; migration tool included.
commits: init: add jurisdictional evaluator core and Rego policies
installer: wire kms scope gate into bootstrap preflight
audit: introduce audit redactor and signed-minimal-envelope
migrate: kms-residency-check migration script and cli helper
tests: unit tests for evaluator + e2e scenario harness
docs: operational guide and upgrade notes
chore: CI workflows for installer e2e and policy lint
description:
Context and motivation: Several regulated customers and our internal compliance review asked that installer-time checks be introduced so that clusters created via the Private Installer cannot accidentally bind operator credentials, KMS keys, or audit exports to an incorrect jurisdiction. Previously the control plane enforced most residency checks at runtime; that leaves a window during bootstrap and migrations where keys can be created with incorrect scope. This PR introduces an installer-side Jurisdictional Access Evaluator that validates RBAC v2 constraint language at install time, enforces KMS key scoping gates, and applies an audit redaction policy for onboarding logs.

Summary of changes: adds a lightweight evaluator component (installer/pkg/evaluator) that runs as part of the preflight/approval step, an OPA Rego policy bundle (installer/policies/jurisdictional.rego) that expresses allowed_jurisdictions and operator-scoped constraints, a KMS scope validator hooked into helm/installer templates, and an audit redactor that strips PII and produces a minimal signed envelope for audit ingest. Also includes a migration helper (scripts/migrate/kms_residency_check.py) to scan existing clusters and surface mismatched KMS keys before upgrades.

Why installer-level: moving enforcement earlier reduces blast radius for misconfigured automation and makes offline/air-gapped installs provably compliant before any keys are provisioned. The evaluator is designed to be declarative: customers can supply constraints in values.yaml or via the private-installer config CR, and the evaluator will fail fast if constraints are violated.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (internal): linear/ENG-7345 (linked)
- [x] Rego policy and unit tests
- [x] Installer integration and preflight gating
- [x] Audit redactor implementation + unit tests
- [x] Migration script for existing clusters
- [x] e2e scenarios covering: correct jurisdiction, cross-jurisdiction key, and rolling upgrade with flagged keys
- [x] Operational docs and upgrade notes

Commits summary: see commits list provided above. Key commits: "init: add jurisdictional evaluator core and Rego policies" introduces the Rego policy model (allowed_jurisdictions, operator_role_constraints, kms_key_label_requirements) and a small interpreter wrapper that validates the cluster config blob. "installer: wire kms scope gate into bootstrap preflight" adds the gating hook that runs evaluator and makes the installer exit 1 with a clear error message and remediation steps. "audit: introduce audit redactor and signed-minimal-envelope" implements a configurable rule set for redacting request/response payload fields and signs a digest with installer-local key to allow audit ingestion services to verify provenance without seeing PII.

Changed areas / rationale for reviewers: the bulk of logic is under installer/pkg/evaluator and installer/policies. KMS scope changes touch pkg/kms and helm templates because installer can now inject labels/annotations required by controllers to tie keys to regions. Audit redaction touches pkg/audit and the chart config to enable the redactor as a sidecar in air-gapped environments. Tests live in tests/e2e and unit tests accompany each package.

Review conversation (summary):
- Luis Ortega (2026-01-22): "Design looks good, two asks: (1) we need a small set of non-regression unit tests for existing installer flows, (2) please document the failure modes in the upgrade notes so SREs can triage broken KMS bindings."
  - Author reply (Nina): "Added unit tests and expanded upgrade notes; included failure codes and remediation steps in docs/operational/compliance/jurisdictional-evaluator.md."
- Aisha Rahman (2026-01-29): "Concern about audit redactor: what fields will be removed and how will that affect downstream billing/usage analytics? Suggest adding a minimized envelope that retains token/usage hashes but not raw content."
  - Author reply: "Implemented signed-minimal-envelope: we keep content hashes + token metadata + jurisdiction tag. Updated tests and ops doc. Added feature flag to opt-out for customers that need full audit logs (enterprise-only)."
- Tomás Becker (2026-02-03): "Found flake in e2e where migration script timed out against slow clusters. Suggest adding retry/backoff and a timeout metric."
  - Author reply: "Added exponential backoff, increased default timeout, and emitted installer metric installer.jurisdictional.migration.duration_ms for observability."

CI notes: Initial CI run (pipeline #4921) failed on gofmt and a Rego linter rule. Fixes applied in follow-up commits. e2e on the first run was flaky (timed out on remote QEMU cluster), retried after adding backoff; final CI run shows all checks passed: unit, linters (rego + go), integration tests, and e2e smoke. Full CI status: pass.

Migration path and upgrade guidance: The migration script scans cluster resources for kms key references and compares key location labels against installer constraints. If mismatches are found the installer will: (a) mark the upgrade as blocked, (b) emit a detailed report to stdout and upload (if enabled) to secure S3 with a signed envelope, and (c) provide remediation suggestions (rebind keys to regional aliases or request operator-scoped re-provision via our KMS reconciliation tool). The docs include a sample remediation playbook.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Default behavior for existing installs is no-op; installer will only enforce jurisdictional checks if a non-empty allowed_jurisdictions block is present in values.yaml or the config CR. The audit redactor is behind a feature flag (values.audit.redactor.enabled) which Enterprise customers can enable during onboarding.

Security review: Sec team (SEC-2021) performed a short review. Recommendations addressed: hardened the redactor to avoid accidental data leakage, added signature validation for signed-minimal-envelopes, and limited the installer-local key lifetime (it is rotated after bootstrap).

Merge outcome: Squash merged into main on 2026-02-13 by Nina Patel. Squash commit message: "installer: enforce jurisdictional evaluator and KMS scope gates; add audit redactor and migration tooling".
